mainTopic: The vicious dog and קהלת 11:9, then which items can become טמא: the בירית, כבלים, and ornaments and woven cloth of any size
overview: The amud opens by finishing a teaching that someone who keeps a vicious dog holds back kindness from his home. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that he also throws off יראת שמים, and a story shows a dog's bark causing a miscarriage. רב הונא and ריש לקיש then give two readings of a verse in קהלת about youthful joy and future judgment. The גמרא returns to the משנה and explains that a בירית is a leg band that corresponds to the arm's אצעדה, so it stays טהורה. רבין and רב הונא debate how a בירית differs from כבלים. רב הונא shows that a chain joining two garters turns them into כבלים, because the chain has a real job: it keeps the wearer's steps short. רב דימי corrects his report of רבי יוחנן's teaching: the ציץ teaches that an ornament of any size can become טמא, and או בגד teaches the same for woven cloth. A ברייתא and רבא add the case of an item that is both woven and an ornament. When רבא's source from מדין is challenged, he begins to answer that the law is learned through a comparison, and that answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why the verse's word למס means a dog
steps.stepSummary: This amud opens partway through a teaching. It explains that ״לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״ refers to a dog, because in Greek a dog is called 'lamas'.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...kindness from his friend.' This verse is about a dog, because in Greek people call a dog 'lamas'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a teaching that someone who keeps a vicious dog holds back kindness from his home. Here it explains why the verse in איוב is talking about a dog at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse says ״לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״, which means 'to the one who melts (withholds) kindness from his friend.' The גמרא reads ״לַמָּס״ as a play on the Greek word for dog. That turns the verse into a warning about the owner of a vicious dog, because poor people and guests are afraid to come to his door, so his home loses the חסד it could have done.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the verse that sounds like the Greek word for 'dog'
The Greek language
Kindness
A vicious dog (the subject of this teaching)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of a sentence. The words ״מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״ are the end of a verse that was quoted just before This amud begins. They are not a new statement.

phrases.english: '...kindness from his friend' —
phrases.notes: End of the verse in איוב 6:14, quoted at the end of the previous section

phrases.english: since in the Greek language
they call a dog 'lamas'.
phrases.notes: A wordplay that links the verse to a dog

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁכֵּן בְּלָשׁוֹן יְוָנִית קוֹרִין לְכֶלֶב לַמָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a derivation that began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse ״לַמָּס מֵרֵעֵהוּ חָסֶד״ refers to someone who keeps a vicious dog, since 'lamas' means dog in Greek.

steps.title: Keeping a vicious dog also throws off fear of Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that keeping a vicious dog removes יראת שמים, based on the end of the same verse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: such a person even throws off fear of Heaven, as the verse says, 'and the fear of the Almighty he will abandon.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק goes one step further than the previous teaching. Keeping a vicious dog does not only hurt kindness; it also hurts the owner's יראת שמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the verse was used to teach that the owner loses חסד. רב נחמן בר יצחק uses the second half, ״וְיִרְאַת שַׁדַּי יַעֲזוֹב״, to add a spiritual cost. The word אַף ('even') shows that he is adding to the earlier teaching, not arguing with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even / also (signals an addition)
Throws off, removes (like taking off a yoke)
Fear of Heaven
The Almighty (a name of God)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
he even throws off from himself fear of Heaven,
as it says: 'And the fear of the Almighty he will abandon.'
phrases.notes: The second half of the same verse in איוב

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק אָמַר אַף פּוֹרֵק מִמֶּנּוּ יִרְאַת שָׁמַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second penalty, drawn from the rest of the same verse
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who keeps a vicious dog also loses יראת שמים.

steps.title: A dog's bark causes a woman to miscarry
steps.stepSummary: A story: a pregnant woman went into a house to bake. The dog barked at her and she miscarried. The owner told her not to fear, since the dog had no teeth or claws.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain woman went into a certain house to bake. The dog barked at her, and her unborn baby was dislodged. The owner of the house said to her: 'Don't be afraid. His teeth and his claws have been removed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that shows how much harm a vicious dog can cause. This part sets up the scene and the owner's reassurance. Her answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner thinks the dog is harmless because it cannot bite or scratch. The damage, however, came from the fear the bark caused, not from any bite. This shows why keeping such a dog is wrong even if it is 'safe' physically.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman
To bake
Barked
Her fetus was dislodged (she miscarried)
The owner of the house
His teeth and his claws

phrases.english: A certain woman who entered
into a certain house to bake.
The dog barked at her,
and her fetus was dislodged.
The owner of the house said to her:
Do not be afraid,
because his teeth have been removed and his claws have been removed.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַהִיא אִיתְּתָא דַּעֲיַילָא לְהָהוּא בֵּיתָא לְמֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a real-life story showing the harm of a vicious dog

steps.title: The woman rejects the owner's reassurance
steps.stepSummary: The woman answers that his comfort is worthless, because the fetus has already been dislodged.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: 'Take your kindness and throw it on the thorns. The baby has already moved.'
steps.whatsHappening: The woman rejects the owner's comfort. This ends the story with its lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her sharp answer shows that removing teeth and claws does not solve the problem. A frightening dog causes harm through fear alone. That backs up the earlier teaching that keeping a vicious dog is a serious matter.

keyTerms.meaning: Your goodness / favor
Thorns
The fetus has moved (is dislodged)

steps.whatToRemember: A vicious dog can cause serious harm just through fear, even if it cannot bite. This is why חז״ל speak so strongly against keeping a כלב רע.

phrases.english: She said to him:
Take your goodness and throw it on the thorns,
phrases.notes: An idiom meaning 'your help is useless'

phrases.english: the fetus has already moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁקִילָא טֵיבוּתָיךְ וְשַׁדְיָא אַחִיזְרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the owner's claim that the dog is harmless
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The owner's reassurance that a toothless, clawless dog poses no danger
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The harm came from fright, not from biting, so removing teeth and claws did not help.

steps.title: רב הונא: the verse is first the evil inclination, then the good inclination
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains קהלת 11:9. The first half ('rejoice, follow your heart') is the voice of the יצר הרע, and the second half ('know that God will judge you') is the voice of the יצר טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What does this verse mean: 'Rejoice, young man, in your youth, let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth, and walk in the ways of your heart and the sight of your eyes; but know that for all these God will bring you to judgment'? Up to this point, these are the words of the evil inclination. From here on, these are the words of the good inclination.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic. רב הונא explains a verse in קהלת by splitting it into two voices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first half of the verse sounds like encouragement to follow every desire. רב הונא says that half is the יצר הרע speaking. The second half, the warning about judgment, is the יצר טוב answering it. This explains how one verse can seem to say two opposite things.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written? (opens a verse explanation)
The evil inclination
The good inclination
Up to here / from here on (divides a text into parts)

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
What is the meaning of that which is written:
'Rejoice, young man, in your youth,
and let your heart cheer you in the days of your youth,
and walk in the ways of your heart and in the sight of your eyes;
but know that for all these things
God will bring you to judgment' (קהלת 11:9) —
up to here are the words of the evil inclination;
from here on are the words of the good inclination.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא מַאי דִכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new, loosely related aggadic topic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In קהלת 11:9, the call to follow one's heart is the יצר הרע speaking, and the warning of judgment is the יצר טוב.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the verse is first Torah study, then good deeds
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the same verse differently. The first half refers to joyful Torah study, and the second half refers to good deeds, for which a person will be judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: Up to this point, the verse is about Torah study. From here on, it is about good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives a different way to split the same verse. Both halves are positive in his reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For ריש לקיש, 'rejoice in your youth' means enjoy learning Torah while young. 'Know that God will judge you' means you will be held responsible for actually doing what you learned. So the verse is not a battle between two inclinations; it is a call to both learn and act.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא in ארץ ישראל, the study partner of רבי יוחנן
Words of Torah / Torah study
Good deeds

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume ריש לקיש agrees that the first half is bad advice. In his reading, 'rejoice in your youth' is a good thing: the joy of learning Torah.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of קהלת 11:9. רב הונא sees the יצר הרע and then the יצר טוב. ריש לקיש sees Torah study and then good deeds, so learning must lead to action.

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
up to here, it refers to matters of Torah;
from here on, it refers to good deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר עַד כָּאן לְדִבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the same verse that רב הונא explained
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first half of קהלת 11:9 refers to Torah study, and the second half refers to good deeds, for which one will be judged.
steps.whyThisMatters: ריש לקיש's reading teaches that Torah learning brings responsibility. A person will be judged on whether he carried out what he learned.

steps.title: רב יהודה defines the garter as a bracelet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'a בירית is טהורה,' and רב יהודה explains that a בירית is an אצעדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A garter is pure.' רב יהודה said: This garter is a bracelet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and asks what a בירית is. רב יהודה gives a definition: it is an אצעדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said a בירית is טהורה, meaning it cannot become ritually impure, and that a woman may go out with it on שבת. רב יהודה identifies the object by linking it to a familiar item, the אצעדה. As stated, his words sound like the two objects are identical, and that sets up the next challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: A garter, a band worn on the leg
Pure, meaning it cannot become ritually impure
A bracelet worn on the arm

phrases.english: A garter is pure.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
Garter: this is a bracelet.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּירִית טְהוֹרָה. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the aggadic discussion of קהלת and returns to explaining a term in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בירית is identified with an אצעדה.

steps.title: רב יוסף objects: a bracelet can become impure
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points out that the משנה calls a בירית טהורה, while an אצעדה is known to be טמאה. So the two cannot be the same object.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged: The משנה says a garter is pure and a woman may go out with it on שבת. But a bracelet can become impure!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks רב יהודה's definition. The two objects have opposite טומאה rules, so they cannot be the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה lists the אצעדה among the spoils of מדין (במדבר 31:50), and those spoils needed purification. That shows an אצעדה can become טמא. If a בירית were simply an אצעדה, the משנה could not call it טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a source
Whereas, but in contrast
Able to become ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not saying a בירית is a forbidden burden on שבת. His challenge is only about טומאה: the משנה calls the בירית טהורה, but an אצעדה can become טמאה.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
A garter is pure, and one may go out with it on Shabbat,
whereas a bracelet is impure!
phrases.notes: Based on the spoils of מדין, which needed purification

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's definition from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's statement that a בירית is an אצעדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two objects cannot be identical if one is טהורה (per the משנה) and the other is טמאה (per the spoils of מדין).

steps.title: The garter takes the place of a bracelet
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רב יהודה. He did not mean the two are the same object. He meant the בירית is worn on the leg the way an אצעדה is worn on the arm.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he meant: A garter stands in place of a bracelet.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה by explaining his words differently. He was comparing the two objects, not equating them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a בירית and an אצעדה are bands that go around a limb, so רב יהודה used the bracelet to describe the garter's shape and position. They remain different objects. The garter only holds up a stocking and is not an ornament, so it stays טהורה, unlike the bracelet.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he meant (a rereading of someone's words)
In place of, corresponding to
Stands, serves as

steps.whatToRemember: A בירית is a leg band that corresponds to the arm's bracelet. Because it is not the same object as an אצעדה, it keeps its own status of טהורה.

phrases.english: This is what he is saying:
A garter stands in place of a bracelet.
phrases.notes: On the leg, as a bracelet is on the arm

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's objection in step 8 by reinterpreting רב יהודה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יהודה meant that a בירית and an אצעדה are the same object.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יהודה meant that the בירית is the leg's counterpart to the arm's bracelet. They are similar in form but different objects with different טומאה rules.

steps.title: רבין explains how a garter differs from ankle chains
steps.stepSummary: A short story sets the scene: רבין and רב הונא sat before רב ירמיה, who was dozing. רבין then said a בירית is worn on one leg, while כבלים are worn on two.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין and רב הונא were sitting before רב ירמיה, and רב ירמיה was dozing. רבין said: A garter is on one leg; ankle chains are on two legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story in order to introduce רבין's statement. רבין explains the difference between a בירית, which the משנה calls טהורה, and כבלים, which the משנה calls טמאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules differently on the בירית and the כבלים, so we need to know what separates them. רבין says the difference is in how they are worn. A בירית is a band on one leg, while כבלים are worn on both legs. The note that רב ירמיה was dozing sets up the story, which continues in the next lines.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting
Before him, in his presence
Dozing, half-asleep
Ankle chains, worn on both legs

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a practical way to tell apart two items that the משנה treats in opposite ways for טומאה and for going out on שבת.

phrases.english: Ravin and Rav Huna were sitting
before Rav Yirmeya,
and Rav Yirmeya was sitting and dozing.
And Ravin sat and said:
A garter is on one leg,
ankle chains are on two.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רָבִין וְרַב הוּנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having defined the בירית against the אצעדה, the גמרא now separates it from כבלים, the next item in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בירית is worn on one leg; כבלים are worn on two legs.

steps.title: רב הונא: Both are worn on two legs, and a chain makes them כבלים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא disagrees with רבין. Both בירית and כבלים are worn on two legs. When a chain is attached between the two בירית, they become כבלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: These and those are both worn on two legs, and they put a chain between them, and they become ankle chains.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רבין's statement from the last step. He says the difference between בירית and כבלים is not one leg versus two legs, because both are worn on two legs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבין said the difference is one leg against two legs. רב הונא says the real difference is the chain: two בירית with no chain are still בירית, and once a chain links them they become כבלים. This matters because the משנה treats a בירית as טהורה, while כבלים are a כלי that can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: These and those. Here it means both the בירית and the כבלים.
On two, meaning on both legs.
They place or attach.
A chain.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
phrases.notes: He is answering רבין from the story in the previous step.

phrases.english: these and those are both on two legs,
phrases.notes: Both the garters and the ankle chains are worn on both legs.

phrases.english: and they place a chain between them
phrases.notes: A chain connects the two garters.

phrases.english: and they become ankle chains.
phrases.notes: With the chain added, the object now counts as כבלים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא: אֵלּוּ וְאֵלּוּ בִּשְׁתַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different definition from רבין's. The difference is the chain, not the number of legs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both בירית and כבלים are worn on two legs. A chain connecting the two בירית turns them into כבלים.

steps.title: How can a chain turn the garters into a vessel?
steps.stepSummary: רבין challenges רב הונא. If a בירית by itself is not a כלי, why would adding a chain make it into one?
steps.simpleTranslation: And does the chain on it make it into a vessel?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין, still in conversation with רב הונא, questions רב הונא's idea. A chain is just an extra piece, so why should it change the object's status?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a בירית is טהורה, which means it is not treated as a כלי that can become טמא. רב הונא says that adding a chain makes the object כבלים, which can become טמא. The challenge is that the chain does not seem to change what the object is or what it does.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes it into, or gives it the status of.
A vessel or utensil (Aramaic for כְּלִי). Only a כלי can become טמא.

phrases.english: And the chain that is on it
phrases.notes: The chain connecting the two garters.

phrases.english: makes it into a vessel?
phrases.notes: This is a challenge in question form: why should a chain change its status?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשַׁלְשֶׁלֶת שֶׁבּוֹ מְשַׁוְּיָא לֵיהּ מָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב הונא's claim that the chain is what turns the object into כבלים.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that attaching a chain makes the garters into כבלים, an object that can become טמא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בירית alone is טהורה because it is not a כלי. Adding a chain does not seem to change what the object is, so it should not create the status of a כלי.

steps.title: Suggested answer: a metal object that makes noise counts as a vessel
steps.stepSummary: רבין anticipates a possible answer: maybe the chain makes it a כלי because it rattles. רבי שמואל בר נחמני, quoting רבי יוחנן, learns from a פסוק that a metal object which makes sound counts as a כלי and can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say this follows רבי שמואל בר נחמני, as רבי שמואל בר נחמני said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that a metal object which makes a sound can become impure? Because it says, 'Every thing that comes into the fire.' Even speech (sound) is included.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין raises a possible way to defend רב הונא, as part of his challenge. The chain makes noise, and there is a teaching that noise-making metal objects count as a כלי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן reads the word 'דבר' (thing) in the פסוק as hinting to 'דיבור' (speech, meaning sound). So a metal object that makes sound is included among objects that need purifying, which means it can become טמא. The suggestion is that the chain's rattling turns the בירית into such an object. The phrase 'וכי תימא' warns us that רבין is about to reject this suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. It introduces a suggested answer that the גמרא usually goes on to reject.
Something that makes a sound.
Metal vessels or objects.
Ritually impure, or able to become impure.
Speech. Here it means sound, a play on the word דָּבָר in the פסוק.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the גמרא's final answer. 'וכי תימא' means 'you might suggest this.' The next step shows why it does not work here.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי תֵּימָא כְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי,
phrases.english: And if you will say it is like Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani,
phrases.notes: A suggested answer to the challenge.

phrases.english: as Rabbi Shmuel bar Nachmani said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting his teacher.

phrases.english: From where do we know that something that makes a sound
phrases.notes: The question that the פסוק will answer.

phrases.english: among metal objects can become impure?
phrases.notes: A noisy metal object counts as a כלי.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Every thing
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:23, about purifying the spoils of מדין.

phrases.english: that comes into the fire'
phrases.notes: Objects that need purifying through fire.

phrases.english: even speech (sound) is included.
phrases.notes: The word דָּבָר is read as דִּיבּוּר, so sound-makers are included.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא כְּרַבִּי שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר נַחְמָנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the challenge in step 12: the chain's sound might create the status of a כלי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Suggested answer from an outside source (later rejected)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A chain should not change an object's status.
steps.terutzMaskana: Maybe it does, because a metal object that makes sound counts as a כלי according to רבי יוחנן's reading of 'כל דבר'.

steps.title: Rejected: there the sound has a purpose, but here it does nothing
steps.stepSummary: רבין rejects the suggestion. In רבי יוחנן's case, people want the sound and it does a job. Here, what job does the chain's noise do?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense there, because they want the sound and it performs an action. But here, what action does it perform?
steps.whatsHappening: רבין shows that the comparison to noisy metal objects does not work. The next step answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making noise is not enough by itself. The rule about noisy objects applies when the sound is the useful purpose of the object, such as a bell. A chain between garters seems to make noise for no reason, so it should not count as a כלי. The question 'what action does it do?' is left for the גמרא to answer next.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense, granted. It sets up a contrast: this works there, but not here.
There and here. It compares the earlier case to the current one.
Sound.
An action, a real useful function.

steps.whatToRemember: An object counts as a כלי because of its sound only when the sound has a real use. So the גמרא still needs to explain what useful job the chain on the garters does.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets an important principle for טומאה: a feature makes something a כלי only if it serves a purpose. It also sets up the next step, where the גמרא explains the chain's purpose.

phrases.english: It makes sense there,
phrases.notes: In רבי יוחנן's case of a noise-making object.

phrases.english: because they want it for its sound,
and it performs an action,
but here, what action does it perform?
phrases.notes: The chain's noise seems to do nothing useful. The next step answers this question.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא הָתָם קָא בָעוּ לַהּ לְקָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer from step 13 by showing that the two cases are different.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using רבי שמואל בר נחמני's teaching to explain why the chain creates the status of a כלי.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In that teaching, the sound is useful and is the object's purpose. Here the chain's sound seems to have no purpose, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: The chain has a real purpose: it keeps the girls' steps short
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the rejection in step 14. The chain does do a job, because it shortens the wearer's steps. This is shown from a story told by רבי יוחנן about a family in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, the chain does a useful job. רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: There was a family in ירושלים whose daughters took very large steps, and because of this their signs of virginity would be lost. So the family made them כבלים and put a chain between them. That way their steps would not be so large, and their signs of virginity were no longer lost.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers רבין. He shows that the chain between the two בירית has a real use: it stops the wearer from taking big steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 14 asked what job the chain's noise does. This answer changes the focus from the noise to the chain itself. The chain limits how far the legs can move, and that is a real job. Since it does a job, it makes sense that it turns the pair of בירית into a כלי.

keyTerms.meaning: It does a useful job, it serves a real purpose
Large, wide steps
Signs of virginity
A chain

steps.confusionAlert: The answer is not about the noise anymore. Step 13 tried to rely on the sound and step 14 rejected that. The new answer is that the chain's physical job of limiting steps is what counts.

phrases.english: Here too, it does perform a useful action,
phrases.notes: This directly answers the challenge of step 14.

phrases.english: as Rabba bar bar Chana said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
There was one family in Jerusalem
whose (daughters') steps were large
and their signs of virginity would fall away.
They made them leg-bands (כבלים)
and attached a chain between them,
so that their steps would not be large,
and their signs of virginity no longer fell away.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא נָמֵי קָא עָבֵיד מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the rejection in step 14 by showing that the chain does have a real function.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows that a function exists, which the challenge said was missing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chain seemed to do nothing useful, so it should not be able to make the בירית into a כלי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chain limits the length of the wearer's steps. That useful job lets it turn the בירית into כבלים, which are a כלי.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה wakes up and agrees with רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה, who had been dozing, wakes up and approves of what was said. He adds that רבי יוחנן said the same thing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה woke up from their voices and said to them: Well said! And רבי יוחנן said the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The story from step 10 is wrapped up. רבי ירמיה wakes up and confirms that רב הונא's view is right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This closes the discussion about בירית and כבלים. Two leg-bands joined by a chain are כבלים. The chain makes them a כלי because it does a real job. רבי ירמיה's approval, backed by רבי יוחנן, settles the matter in favor of רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: He woke up
Well said, correct (literally: may your strength be straight)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's view is accepted. בירית are worn on both legs, and a chain joining them turns them into כבלים. The chain makes them a כלי because it does a real job: it keeps the steps short.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya woke up because of them (their voices),
and said to them: Well said!
And so too said Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּעַר בְּהוּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the frame story from step 10 and confirms the answer given in step 15.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is correct. כבלים are two בירית joined by a chain, and the chain's job of limiting the steps makes them a כלי.

steps.title: Woven cloth of any size can become טמא, learned from the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: A new topic begins. רב דימי reports that רבי יוחנן learns from the ציץ of the כהן גדול that woven cloth of any size can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came from ארץ ישראל, he said in the name of רבי יוחנן: From where do we know that a woven item of any size can become טמא? From the ציץ.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic about טומאה. רבי יוחנן says that even a tiny piece of woven material can become טמא, and his source is the ציץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a piece of cloth must reach a certain minimum size before it can become טמא. רבי יוחנן says that a woven item of any size can become טמא. His proof is the ציץ, which was small but still counted as a real item that could become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
A woven item
Of any size, even the smallest
The gold plate worn on the forehead of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came (from Eretz Yisrael),
he said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
From where do we know that a woven item of any size
can become impure?
From the tzitz (the High Priest's forehead plate).

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about טומאה, loosely connected to the earlier discussion of what counts as a כלי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woven item of any size can become טמא. The source is the ציץ.

steps.title: אביי objects: the ציץ was a gold plate, not woven cloth
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב דימי. A ברייתא describes the ציץ as a plate of gold, so how can it be the source for a law about woven items?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is the ציץ woven?! But a ברייתא teaches: The ציץ was like a plate of gold, two fingers wide, and it went around the forehead from ear to ear. Written on it in two lines were the letters of the שם, יוד הא, on top, and קודש למ״ד (meaning 'holy to') below.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks the source that רב דימי gave for רבי יוחנן's rule. He quotes a ברייתא showing that the ציץ was made of gold, not woven material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's proof only works if the ציץ was woven. The ברייתא clearly describes it as a smooth gold plate. If so, how can we learn anything about woven cloth from it? The ברייתא also explains how the words קודש לה׳ were arranged: the שם was placed on the upper line out of respect.

keyTerms.meaning: But a ברייתא teaches (introduces a source that challenges what was said)
A plate of gold
Going around the head from ear to ear
Lines of writing

steps.confusionAlert: 'יוד הא' and 'קודש למ״ד' are not separate words. Together they spell קודש לה׳, 'holy to ה׳.' The שם was written on the top line out of respect, and 'קודש ל' was written underneath it.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Is the tzitz a woven item?!
But it was taught in a baraita:
The tzitz is like a kind of gold plate,
and it is two fingerbreadths wide,
and it goes around from ear to ear,
and written on it in two lines is:
'Yud Heh' (God's Name) above,
and 'Kodesh Lamed' ('holy to') below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְצִיץ אָרִיג הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source given in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's use of the ציץ as the source for the rule about woven items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ציץ was a solid gold plate, not something woven. So it cannot teach a law about woven cloth.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי saw the ציץ in רומי with one line of writing
steps.stepSummary: Still inside the ברייתא, רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי adds that he saw the ציץ in רומי, and קודש לה׳ was written on it in a single line.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי said: I saw it in רומי, and קודש לה׳ was written on it in one line.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is a side comment within the same ברייתא that אביי quoted. It disagrees about how the writing was arranged, but it agrees that the ציץ was a gold plate. The next step answers אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר ברבי יוסי reports what he saw with his own eyes: all the words were on one line, not two. This is a disagreement about the writing only. Either way, the ברייתא still shows that the ציץ was metal, so אביי's challenge still stands until רב דימי answers it in step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: Rome, where the ציץ was taken after the destruction of the בית המקדש
'Holy to ה׳,' the words engraved on the ציץ
One line of writing

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer, son of Rabbi Yosei, said:
I saw it in Rome,
and written on it was 'Holy to ה׳'
in one line.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי: אֲנִי רְאִיתִיו בְּרוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא quoted in step 18 with a side opinion about how the writing was arranged.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to an eyewitness, קודש לה׳ was written on the ציץ in a single line.

steps.title: רב דימי admits his mistake and gives the correct version
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי sends word that his earlier report was wrong. רבי יוחנן really learned ornaments from the ציץ, and woven cloth from או בגד.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי went up to נהרדעא, he sent them this message: 'What I told you was my mistake. This is what they really said in the name of רבי יוחנן. How do we know that an ornament of any size can become טמא? From the ציץ. How do we know that woven cloth of any size can become טמא? From the words "או בגד" ("or a garment").'
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי takes back his earlier report, so אביי's question no longer applies. He then gives the corrected teaching of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי had asked how a gold plate could teach a law about woven cloth. רב דימי agrees that it cannot, so he splits the teaching in two. The ציץ, which is a metal ornament, teaches about ornaments. The פסוק או בגד teaches about woven cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: נהרדעא, a major Torah center in בבל
They are my mistake (I reported them wrongly)
An ornament or piece of jewelry
Of any size, even the tiniest amount
'Or a garment', words from the פסוק about שרצים (ויקרא יא:לב)

steps.whatToRemember: The corrected version has two separate sources. The ציץ teaches about ornaments. או בגד teaches about woven cloth.
steps.confusionAlert: רב דימי is not saying that רבי יוחנן made a mistake. He is saying that he himself reported רבי יוחנן's words incorrectly.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that an אמורא can openly admit a mistake in passing on a teaching. It also gives us the basic sources that the rest of the section builds on.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi went up to Neharde'a
he sent word to them:
The things that I told you
are a mistake on my part,
phrases.notes: He is taking back what he said about woven cloth being learned from the ציץ.

phrases.aramaic: בְּרַם כָּךְ אָמְרוּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: but this is what they said in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
From where do we know that an ornament of any size
can become impure? From the frontplate (ציץ).
phrases.notes: The ציץ was a very small gold ornament, yet it counted as a כלי.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that woven cloth of any size
can become impure? From "or a garment."
phrases.notes: The extra word 'או' includes any garment, no matter how small.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּבָרִים שֶׁאָמַרְתִּי לָכֶם טָעוּת הֵם בְּיָדִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves אביי's challenge (steps 18-19) by retracting the original report and replacing it.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Retraction and correction of the reported tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן learned that woven cloth of any size is טמא from the ציץ.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ציץ teaches about ornaments, and או בגד teaches about woven cloth.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ornaments of any size can become טמא (from the ציץ), and woven cloth of any size can become טמא (from או בגד).

steps.title: A ברייתא teaches the same rules and adds more
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that woven cloth, ornaments, and items that are a mix of both can become טמא at any size. It also says that a שק is treated like a garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: Woven cloth of any size can become טמא. An ornament of any size can become טמא. Something that is both woven and an ornament, of any size, can become טמא. A שק is added to the category of garment, and it is טמא because it is woven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches רב דימי's corrected version. It also adds new cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists woven cloth and ornaments as two separate categories, just as in the corrected version. It adds a third case: an item made of both woven cloth and ornament together. It also teaches that a שק counts like a בגד, since it is woven too.

keyTerms.meaning: Woven cloth or fabric
An item that is part woven cloth and part ornament
Added (included in the same category)
Sackcloth, usually woven from goat hair

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Woven cloth of any size can become impure,
and an ornament of any size can become impure.
Something woven and ornament together, of any size, can become impure.
phrases.notes: For example, a piece of cloth with a small ornament attached to it.

phrases.english: A sack is added on to the category of garment
since it is impure because it is woven.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that agrees with רב דימי's corrected version and expands it.
steps.raayaObject: The corrected version, which treats woven cloth and ornaments as separate categories
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Woven cloth, ornaments, and items mixing the two can all become טמא at any size. A שק is included because it is woven.

steps.title: רבא gives a source for each rule in the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רבא matches each rule to a source: או בגד for woven cloth, the ציץ for ornaments, and כל כלי מעשה for the mixed item.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Woven cloth of any size is טמא, as we learn from 'או בגד'. An ornament of any size is טמא, as we learn from the ציץ. Something both woven and an ornament, of any size, is טמא, as we learn from 'כל כלי מעשה' ('every crafted vessel').
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains the ברייתא by giving a פסוק or source for each of its three rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two sources are the same ones רב דימי gave. The new piece is the mixed item. רבא learns it from the words כל כלי מעשה, which appear in the פסוק about the gold jewelry taken from מדין (במדבר לא:נא). Those words show that anything that is a crafted, usable item is included.

keyTerms.meaning: רבא, a leading אמורא of בבל
'Every crafted vessel', words from the פסוק about the spoils of מדין (במדבר לא:נא)

steps.whyThisMatters: רבא's choice of the מדין פסוק for the mixed item is exactly what the next step challenges.

phrases.english: Rava said:

phrases.aramaic: אָרִיג כׇּל שֶׁהוּא טָמֵא — מֵ״אוֹ בֶגֶד״.
phrases.english: Woven cloth of any size is impure, from "or a garment."
An ornament of any size is impure, from the frontplate.
Woven and ornament together, of any size, is impure:
from "every crafted vessel."
phrases.notes: These words come from במדבר לא:נא, about the gold taken from מדין.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a scriptural source for each rule in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Woven cloth comes from או בגד, ornaments come from the ציץ, and the mixed item comes from כל כלי מעשה.

steps.title: One of the חכמים objects that רבא's verse is about מדין
steps.stepSummary: One of the חכמים challenges רבא. The פסוק כל כלי מעשה is written about מדין, so how can it teach a general law of טומאה?
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים said to רבא: That פסוק is written about מדין!
steps.whatsHappening: One of the חכמים attacks רבא's source for the mixed item. This sets up the next move, where רבא must defend his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק כל כלי מעשה is part of the story of the war with מדין, where the topic is טומאת מת. The challenge is that a פסוק in that setting may not be able to teach general rules about which items can become טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the חכמים (an unnamed scholar)
מדין, the nation that ישראל fought in במדבר לא
It is written

phrases.english: One of the Rabbis said to Rava:
That verse is written about Midian!
phrases.notes: The context there is purifying the spoils from טומאת מת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the third source given by רבא in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's use of כל כלי מעשה as the source for an item that is both woven and an ornament
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק belongs to the story of מדין and its טומאת מת, so it may not apply to טומאה law in general.

steps.title: רבא answers that the law is derived through a comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers the challenge: the law is not read off the מדין פסוק on its own terms. Instead, it is derived ('גָּמַר') by linking it to another source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: He derived it (through a comparison to another פסוק).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins his answer to the חכם who asked how a פסוק about מדין can teach a general law. This line opens the answer. The exact comparison רבא has in mind comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question was that כל כלי מעשה is said about the spoils of מדין, so it seems limited to that event. רבא's word "גָּמַר" signals a גזירה שוה, a link between two פסוקים that share a word. Through that link, the rule spreads beyond מדין to the general laws of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him. Introduces a reply to the person who just spoke.
He derived / he learned it out. Usually points to a גזירה שוה.
A verbal analogy. A law is carried from one פסוק to another because they share the same word.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא is saying the מדין פסוק directly teaches the general law. His point is the opposite: on its own it would be limited to מדין. It becomes general only because it is linked to another source.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: He derived it
phrases.notes: Here גָּמַר means he learned it through a גזירה שוה, the same word showing up in two places. The גמרא spells out that word next.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גָּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge in Step 23. That challenge asked how a פסוק about מדין can teach general טומאה law.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Source mechanism. The rule is extended through a גזירה שוה rather than read straight from the context of מדין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger assumed that כל כלי מעשה applies only to the spoils of מדין and cannot teach a general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא holds that the rule is derived ('גָּמַר') by linking it to another source. That link makes it a general law of טומאה.
